tracks.narration: Three wires meet at a single point — where does all the charge go?
Here's a node: one wire bringing five amps in, two wires carrying current out — three amps one way, two the other.
Watch the charge dots stream in from the top. Five dots arrive every second. Three peel off to the right, two go left. Nothing piles up.
Sum of currents in equals sum of currents out, at every node. Five equals three plus two. That's Kirchhoff's current law.
It's just charge conservation: a node is a wire, not a bucket — what arrives must leave.
